AN ACT to amend the public authorities law, in relation to the New York power

items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S2462

SPONSOR: GIANARIS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the public authorities law, in relation to the New York
power authority's conferral process

 
PURPOSE:

This bill requires regular updates on the New York Power Authority's
work to build public renewables and added transparency requirements
around their annual conferral process.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section one of the bill sets the short title as the "Public Renewables
Transparency Act."

Section two of the bill amends subdivision 27-a of § 1005 of the public
authorities law, as amended by § 28 of part 0 of chapter 58 of the laws
of 2024, to require reports on public renewable development at each
board of trustees' meeting.

Section three of the bill amends subdivision 27-a of § 1005 of the
public authorities law, as amended by § 1 of part QQ of chapter 56 of
the laws of 2023, to require reports on public renewable development at
each board of trustees' meeting.

Section four of the bill amends subparagraph (vii) of paragraph (e) of
subdivision 27-a of § 1005 of the public authorities law to specify
October eleventh as the date for the authority to publish a draft of the
strategic plan for at least sixty days to receive public comments,
increasing the number of public hearings from at least three to at least
six, providing an option for stakeholders to submit feedback remotely,
and requiring the authority to incorporate feedback from the public
hearings and feed back into the final draft of the strategic plan.

Section five of the bill sets the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

As the New York Power Authority begins to implement the Build Public
Renewables provisions from the FY2024 budget, various stakeholders
inside and outside of government are interested in seeing additional
transparency in the conferral process and the implementation of the
resulting strategic plan.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2024: S9005-A (Gianaris) PASSED SENATE / A9538-A (Shrestha) died in
energy

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately, provided that the amendments to
paragraph (d) of subdivision 27-a of section 1005 of the public authori-
ties law made by section two of this act shall be subject to the expira-
tion and reversion of such paragraph pursuant to section 34 of part 0 of
chapter 58 of the laws of 2024, as amended, when upon such date the
provisions of section three of this act shall take effect.

A.lawCode: Amd §1005, Pub Auth L; amd §6-102, Energy L
A.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S2462A

SPONSOR: GIANARIS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the public authorities law and the energy law, in
relation to the New York power authority's conferral process

 
PURPOSE:

This bill requires regular updates on the New York Power Authority's
work to build public renewables and added transparency requirements
around their annual conferral process.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section one of the bill sets the short title as the "Public Renewables
Transparency Act."

Section two of the bill amends paragraph (d) of subdivision 27-a of §
1005 of the public authorities law, as amended by § 28 of part 0 of
chapter 58 of the laws of 2024, to require reports on public renewable
development at each board of trustees' meeting, as well as a public
dashboard demonstrating their progress in implementing the authority's
renewable energy generation strategic plan.

Section three of the bill amends paragraph (d) of subdivision 27-a of §
1005 of the public authorities law, as amended by § 1 of part QQ of
chapter 56 of the laws of 2023, to require reports on public renewable
development at each board of trustees' meeting and to maintain a public
dashboard demonstrating their progress in implementing the authority's
renewable energy generation strategic plan.

Section four of the bill amends subparagraph (iv) of paragraph (e) of
subdivision 27-a of § 1005 of the public authorities law, as added by §
1 or part QQ of chapter 56 of the laws of 2023, is amended by requiring
the strategic plan to address the state's progress toward CLCPA goals
methodologies and modeling of their financial capabilities, quantitative
assessments of various borrowing scenarios, and the potential for lever-
aging other sources of capital within the authority.

Section five of the bill amends subparagraph (vii) of paragraph (e) of
subdivision 27-a of § 1005 of the public authorities law to specify
October eleventh as the date for the authority to publish a draft of the
strategic plan for at least sixty days to receive public comments. This
section would also increase the number of public hearings from at least
three to at least six, require in-person public hearings to be held in
locations with access to public transit, provide an option for stake-
holders to submit feedback remotely, make the comments public within 5
days after the comment period ends, and require the authority to incor-
porate feedback from the public hearings into the final draft of the
strategic plan.

Section six of the bill amends § 6-102 of the energy law to include the
chief executive officer of the New York Power Authority as a member of
the New York Energy Planning Board.

Section seven of the bill sets the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

As the New York Power Authority begins to implement the Build Public
Renewables provisions from the FY2024 budget, various stakeholders
inside and outside of government are interested in seeing additional
transparency in the conferral process and the implementation of the
resulting strategic plan.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2024: S9005-A (Gianaris) PASSED SENATE / A9538-A (Shrestha) died in
energy

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately, provided that the amendments to
paragraph (d) of subdivision 27-a of section 1005 of the public authori-
ties law made by section two of this act shall be subject to the expira-
tion and reversion of such paragraph pursuant to section 34 of part O of
chapter 58 of the laws of 2024, as amended, when upon such date the
provisions of section three of this act shall take effect.

This bill requires regular updates on the New York Power Authority's
work to build public renewables and added transparency requirements

Section one of the bill sets the short title as the "Public Renewables

1005 of the public authorities law, to require reports on public renewa-
ble development at board of trustees' meeting, as well as a public dash-

eration to locations with access to public transit when selecting
locations for in-person public hearings.

chief executive officer of the New York Power Authority as a member of
the New York Energy Planning Board.

Section five of the bill sets the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

As the New York Power Authority implements the Build Public Renewables
provisions from the FY2024 budget, various stakeholders inside and
outside of government are interested in seeing additional transparency
measures.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2024: S9005-A (Gianaris) PASSED SENATE / A9538-A (Shrestha) died in
energy

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

summary: Enacts the "public renewables transparency act"; relates to the New York power authority's conferral process; requires the conferral report be posted on the authority's website; provides that the authority shall provide an option for stakeholders to submit comments remotely as well, and incorporate feedback from such sessions and written comments into the final draft of the strategic plan; makes related provisions.
